payload.definition:
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Continuous
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.Bochner.Basic
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring

/-!
# Area and energy densities

For the images `v`, `w` of an orthonormal tangent frame under a differential,
the area density is the square root of the Gram determinant and the energy
density is half the sum of the squared norms. The area is bounded by the
energy, with equality precisely for orthogonal vectors of equal norm.

The integral results assume measurable vector fields and integrable energy;
integrability of the area is a conclusion, not an additional assumption.
They apply on any measure space, including a restricted domain measure.
Identifying these fields with a Sobolev differential on a surface remains a
separate geometric interface. No global frame on the sphere is asserted.

Reference: Colding-Minicozzi, *Width and Finite Extinction Time of Ricci Flow*,
arXiv:0707.0108v1, equation (1.4) and the following equality discussion, p. 3.
https://arxiv.org/pdf/0707.0108v1#page=3
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

open MeasureTheory
open scoped InnerProductSpace

namespace OpenGA

variable {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [InnerProductSpace ℝ F]

/-- **Math.** The two-dimensional Jacobian density of a pair of derivative vectors. -/
noncomputable def areaDensity (v w : F) : ℝ :=
  Real.sqrt (‖v‖ ^ 2 * ‖w‖ ^ 2 - ⟪v, w⟫_ℝ ^ 2)

/-- **Math.** The Dirichlet energy density of a pair of derivative vectors. -/
noncomputable def energyDensity (v w : F) : ℝ :=
  (‖v‖ ^ 2 + ‖w‖ ^ 2) / 2















section Integral

variable {X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace X] {μ : Measure X} {v w : X → F}







end Integral

end OpenGA
payload.definition_title: Area and energy densities of a vector pair
payload.natural_language_statement:

$$A(v,w)=\sqrt{\|v\|^2\|w\|^2-\langle v,w\rangle^2},\qquad E(v,w)=\frac{\|v\|^2+\|w\|^2}{2}.$$

This isolates the analytic ingredient in the surface area-energy comparison. Identifying the vector fields with the differential of a Sobolev surface map, and proving invariance under changes of orthonormal frame, are separate geometric tasks.

This is the vector-pair / measurable-field analytic extraction, not the full Sobolev surface-map statement or the width-equivalence proposition. theorems.explanation:
The area and energy densities agree precisely for orthogonal vectors of equal norm, including the zero pair.

Cauchy-Schwarz makes the Gram determinant nonnegative. Expanding gives

$$E(v,w)^2-A(v,w)^2=\frac{(\|v\|^2-\|w\|^2)^2}{4}+\langle v,w\rangle^2.$$

The two terms on the right are nonnegative. Equality of the densities forces both to vanish. Conversely, orthogonality and equal norms make the right-hand side zero; nonnegativity of both densities then gives equality.

milestone.milestone_description:
For vectors $v,w$ in a real inner product space, define the area density and energy density by

$$A(v,w)=\sqrt{\|v\|^2\|w\|^2-\langle v,w\rangle^2},\qquad E(v,w)=\frac{\|v\|^2+\|w\|^2}{2}.$$

Let $(X,\mu)$ be a measure space and let $v,w:X\to F$ be almost-everywhere strongly measurable fields with integrable energy density $x\mapsto E(v(x),w(x))$. Then

$$\int_X A(v(x),w(x))\,d\mu\leq\int_X E(v(x),w(x))\,d\mu.$$

No finiteness assumption on the measure is needed; finite energy is explicit. This isolates the analytic ingredient in the surface area-energy comparison. Identifying the vector fields with the differential of a Sobolev surface map, and proving invariance under changes of orthonormal frame, are separate geometric tasks.
milestone.title: Area-energy comparison for finite-energy vector fields

theorems.explanation:
For almost-everywhere strongly measurable fields with finite energy, we prove

$$\int_X A(v,w)\,d\mu\leq\int_X E(v,w)\,d\mu.$$

Cauchy-Schwarz and the identity

$$E(v,w)^2-A(v,w)^2=\frac{(\|v\|^2-\|w\|^2)^2}{4}+\langle v,w\rangle^2.$$

show that the area density lies between zero and the energy density at every point. The area density is a continuous function of the pair of vectors, hence is almost-everywhere strongly measurable. Domination by the integrable energy density makes the area density integrable. Monotonicity of the integral gives the assertion.

milestone.milestone_description:
For vectors $v,w$ in a real inner product space, define the area density and energy density by

$$A(v,w)=\sqrt{\|v\|^2\|w\|^2-\langle v,w\rangle^2},\qquad E(v,w)=\frac{\|v\|^2+\|w\|^2}{2}.$$

Let $(X,\mu)$ be a measure space and let $v,w:X\to F$ be almost-everywhere strongly measurable fields with integrable energy density. Then

$$\int_X A(v(x),w(x))\,d\mu=\int_X E(v(x),w(x))\,d\mu$$

holds exactly when

$$\langle v(x),w(x)\rangle=0\quad\text{and}\quad\|v(x)\|=\|w(x)\|\quad\text{for }\mu\text{-almost every }x.$$

This isolates the analytic ingredient in the surface area-energy comparison. Identifying the vector fields with the differential of a Sobolev surface map, and proving invariance under changes of orthonormal frame, are separate geometric tasks.
milestone.title: Equality in the integrated area-energy comparison

theorems.explanation:
Under almost-everywhere strong measurability and integrable energy, equality of total area and energy is equivalent to orthogonality and equal norms almost everywhere.

The pointwise area-energy bound first supplies integrability of the area density by domination. For two integrable functions ordered almost everywhere, equal integrals are equivalent to equality almost everywhere. Applying the proved pointwise equality criterion therefore gives

$$A(v(x),w(x))=E(v(x),w(x))\ \text{a.e.}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \langle v(x),w(x)\rangle=0\ \text{and}\ \|v(x)\|=\|w(x)\|\ \text{a.e.}$$
